cards.issue_title: Adjust eligibility has no Clear button
summary_4_lines: The loan form at the top of Explore banks is filled (existing EMIs ₹555 and the other fields), and they want a way to wipe it.
They ask whether there is a button for that, say every product has one, then accept going on without it.
This continues the same “edit form needs a button” talk from the previous recording.
The form shows See options but no Clear / reset control.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, the expanded Adjust eligibility card has no Clear (or reset) button; at 00:10 they said it is a good idea to clear the form and asked if there is a button, noting everyone has one.
cards.on_screen_object: Adjust eligibility / Loan inputs card (Existing EMIs ₹555, See options) — missing Clear/reset button
quotes_sample: It's a good idea to clear this.
Do you have a button for this?
Everyone has a button like this.
related_discussion_one_liners: After “I accept.” they praise Overview / Charges / Other charges tabs (“These tabs are the best. Columns belong to this tab.”) — praise, not this issue.
Chrome-like tab animation praised in the same stretch.
Sort arrows: “I definitely like this button. Up and down.” — praise.
Filters “Clear all” is a different control; they did not click it.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is a missing Clear/reset on the filled Adjust eligibility form, not Apply-once placement, banks-vs-lenders wording, asterisks on figures, footer English, or named-bank search.

cards.issue_title: Exact rates and loan amounts shown without a star
summary_4_lines: The results table prints exact rates (8.75%, 8.80%) and odd exact loan amounts (₹47,92,101) with no asterisk.
They say that exact figure without a star, then that they will put a star — including in charges — so the site stands behind the number.
They also notice age caps changing how much loan appears (₹5,000 / ₹15,000 / ₹20,000 in speech) while looking at those cells.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks Overview, exact Rate and Loan amount figures are shown without a star; at 02:07 they said the site has taken an exact amount without a star (8.7, 8.8) and that they will put a star, including in charges.
cards.on_screen_object: Bank options table cells: Rate (8.75%, 8.80%) and Loan amount (₹48,00,000 vs Bank of Maharashtra ₹47,92,101) — no asterisk/footnote
quotes_sample: They have taken an exact amount without a star.
So I will put a star.
related_discussion_one_liners: “What is this?” plus spoken “Rs.99.99” / “Rs.7,99” is ASR of the odd ₹47,92,101 amount, not a second issue.
Age restrictions (max 30; if you are 50 you get a smaller loan) explain why amounts differ, still on the same exact-figure problem.
“Charges are okay.” then “At least stand behind something.” / “I don't know if this is a star or not.”
EMI drawer math (exact ₹42,418) is inspecting how an exact EMI is built; they close it; not a separate defect here.
Later More details “How the rate is built” (7.25% = 5.25+2.80−0.80) is related confidence in exact rates, not a new complaint.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is exact Rate and Loan amount cells with no asterisk so the product can stand behind the number, not form Clear, lenders wording, Apply placement, footer English, or bank-name search.

summary_4_lines: They look at the results table and say “Lenders” is the right word.
They want that word used everywhere instead of “banks”.
The table header already says Lenders, but the rest of the page still says banks (Explore banks, Apply once to 33 banks, Show 23 more banks).
This continues the banks-vs-lenders wording talk from the previous recording.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, they said Lenders is a good word and you can put lenders everywhere instead of banks; the column already says Lenders while the page title, Apply once to 33 banks, and Show 23 more banks still say banks.
cards.on_screen_object: Page title / remaining “banks” copy vs table column header “Lenders” (and Apply once / Show more labels that still say banks)
quotes_sample: You can put lenders everywhere instead of banks.
related_discussion_one_liners: “It's okay.” after the instruction — they are not dropping the preference; they are allowing the review to continue.
Search-for-SBI talk later still says “25–30 banks” / “search the bank” (issue-06).
Tab praise just before this is unrelated.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is the product word lenders vs remaining banks copy on title and buttons, not finding a named bank with search, not asterisks on numbers, and not control placement.

cards.issue_title: Apply once is not on top of the row checkboxes
summary_4_lines: After calling the table beautiful, they say Apply should sit here on top of these checkboxes.
The checkboxes are the first column of each bank row; Apply once sits up on the right of the tab bar.
They then select all rows so Apply once lights up, which is the same control they wanted moved.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, Apply once sits on the right of the Overview tab bar rather than on top of the row checkboxes; at 03:17 they said Apply should come here on top of these checkboxes.
cards.on_screen_object: Apply once button (#hlc-apply-btn) vs the bank-row checkboxes in the first table column
quotes_sample: Apply should come here on top of these checkboxes.
related_discussion_one_liners: “Beautiful.” is about the table they are looking at, immediately before the placement instruction.
Selecting all / deselecting is them operating the same checkbox + Apply once system.
The brief apply.html visit (Review your application) is a click-through, not a new complaint in this recording.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is Apply once sitting on the tab bar’s right instead of on top of the row checkboxes, not the eligibility Clear button, lenders wording, or in-page search.

cards.issue_title: “Data last checked on” is not correct English
summary_4_lines: Under the bank table a line reads “Data last checked on 14 July 2026”.
They say that sentence is not correct English and ask for polished English.
They suggest wording like “Accuracy guaranteed” or “updated as of”.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, the line under the table “Data last checked on 14 July 2026” is the sentence they called not correct English (03:32), asking for polished English such as Accuracy guaranteed or updated as of.
cards.on_screen_object: Footer line under the bank table: “Data last checked on 14 July 2026”
quotes_sample: This sentence, data last checked on, is not correct English.
Just make it good polished English.
Something like maybe Accuracy guaranteed or updated as of.
related_discussion_one_liners: Suggested replacements (“Accuracy guaranteed” / “updated as of”) are brainstorming, not extra issues.
“Navani is sorting” / “Are you going to jail?” right after is a side conversation (ASR of a name + joke) while they stay on this page, not a second product defect.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is the table-footer freshness sentence’s English, not asterisks on Rate/Loan cells, lenders vs banks wording, or missing controls.

cards.issue_title: No way on the page to search for a named bank
summary_4_lines: They imagine 25–30 banks on the list and ask how they would find SBI.
There is no search box; they open Floating, show 23 more banks, and talk about cognitive load if search is added.
They say when the list opens, rate should already be sorted lowest to highest, and that Control-F can hold a search instead of a new control.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, with ~10 rows then Show 23 more banks, there is no in-page search for a named bank; at 04:40 they asked how to search for SBI among 25–30 banks, then said a search control is extra cognitive load and Control-F will hold it, with default sort by rate lowest to highest.
cards.on_screen_object: Bank options list (first ~10 rows + “Show 23 more banks”) with no in-page search field for a bank name such as SBI
quotes_sample: Then how do I search for it?
related_discussion_one_liners: “Navani is sorting / going to jail / perfect bank” — side talk, not a second issue.
“Let's see the floating slip” → they click Floating (ASR of the rate-type filter).
“I don't want to show the survey” — ASR; joined with not adding a search UI / extra widget.
“It's like a search symbol” — analogy that sort/rate already works like search.
More details / charges / vertical-vs-horizontal after 06:23 is a new stretch of exploration, mostly praise, not this search issue; next recording continues More details for Bank of Maharashtra.
cards.distinct_from_other_files_in_this_folder: This is missing in-page search for a named bank (SBI) plus cognitive-load / Ctrl+F / default rate-sort talk, not the banks-vs-lenders word, Apply-once placement, or eligibility Clear.
